objective: Characterize outcome-independent equivalence-verifier, exact-binding, and matched-resource schema/tooling on stable main; identify machine-checkable coverage and prospective gaps without touching candidates, outcomes, or scientific workflows.
finding_summary: Stable main already contains strong reusable provenance/file/source binding in release.py and exact authoritative-tag creation/peeled-target verification, but these are not a generic two-run equivalence certificate.

C17 is the strongest reusable exact-equivalence precedent: two independent attested workers, distinct process/hashseed/challenge contracts, parent-side artifact rehashing, exact pre-final bundle comparison, and fail-closed tamper/fabrication tests.

C17 also provides strict one-factor resource-condition validation and bound pre-resource/checkpoint identity checks, while C07 provides experiment-local frozen equivalence tolerances; both remain experiment-specific.

A bounded stable-main inspection found no generic equivalence-certificate schema/tool combining source/protocol/package/input/evaluator identities, privilege/resource envelopes, independent-producer attestations, and ordered semantic stream/checkpoint verification.

The prospective reusable layer should be a pure fail-closed verifier whose decision surface is limited to VALID_EQUIVALENT, VALID_NOT_EQUIVALENT, or INVALID_CONTRACT and carries no candidate/Funnel/scientific authority.
